body:
Opponents of voting rights lack the common sense to understand that these anti-voting conspiracy theories are just flat-out lies. They'd rather see a vast web of shadowy interests arrayed against them than reexamine their own values when they lose elections.
That's why they create bills like the SAVE America, SAVE, and MEGA Acts, to strip our fundamental right to vote until only their select few have the privilege to vote. They simply don't believe we all deserve to vote.
Step up with $35 or more right now to stop the SAVE Act and defend our right to vote from these vicious attacks >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=072726_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
KATU: Vance calls on Congressional Republicans to pass SAVE Act during speech [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=072726_3&amount=25]
Opponents of voting rights are trying everything they can think of to press Congress to advance stalled legislation that purports to address Trump's often-repeated -- and equally debunked -- claims of widespread election fraud. Vice President J.D. Vance called on Congress again recently, begging them to pass this awful bill ahead of the next election.
The SAVE Act was fast-tracked by opponents of voting rights and passed the U.S. House of Representatives. Now, Trump and his MAGA minions are meeting with U.S. Senators, scheming for ways to get this bill through the Senate ahead of November's midterms.
This bill is a stunning assault on our fundamental right to vote, and we can not afford to let this anti-democratic legislation become law, folks.
PITCH IN $35 RIGHT NOW TO STOP THE SAVE ACT NOW ➜ [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=072726_3&amount=35]
Don’t be fooled by the name. This bill would force every voter to present specific types of proof of citizenship to register -- something millions of eligible Americans don’t have on hand. And that’s the point. The bill would also obliterate popular methods of voter registration for all voters, including:
* Registration by mail

* 3rd party voter registration drives

* Online voter registration in states that allow it

* Automatic voter registration
Some estimates say that this bill could disenfranchise up to 11 million eligible Americans , especially women and those who live in under-resourced communities.
“ There’s never been an attack on voting rights out of Congress like this ,” said Alexander Keyssar, a professor of History and Social Policy at the Harvard Kennedy School, and a leading historian of voting rights. “ It’s always been the federal government trying to keep states in check on voting rights, for the most part. ”
Team, the consequences of a bill like this passing would be catastrophic for our democracy. Chip in with $35 or whatever you can today to stop the SAVE Act and other voter suppression bills from becoming law >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=072726_3&amount=35]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:
GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=072726_3&amount=15] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=072726_3&amount=25] GIVE $50 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=072726_3&amount=50]

How do we know non-citizen voting is a made up problem? Because red states and conservative-leaning institutions have spent millions in taxpayer money and donor dollars searching for it and finding minimal results.
For example: The pro-Trump Heritage Foundation -- an organization that has funded anti-voting initiatives for decades -- maintains a database of "election crimes." Their own records only list 24 instances of non-citizens voting in U.S. elections from 2003 to 2023 . In other words -- 20 years of elections, millions of votes, and only 24 alleged non-citizen voters.
The conservative CATO Institute says it best: " These investigations affirm what is simply common sense. People largely aren’t willing to risk their status in the United States — the land of economic opportunity — for the ability to cast one more vote out of hundreds of thousands or millions in a state and hundreds of millions in the country. "
Team, the lies aren't going to stop, but we can push back and make sure bills like this abomination never pass. Pitch in $35 or however much you can to stand against voter suppression bills in Congress and beyond >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=072726_3&amount=35]

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

_Prineville Cooperators Meeting, July 27, 2026_ [>>>>>> CENTRAL OREGON FIRE INFO WEBSITE FOR UPDATES <<<<<<](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fcentraloregonfire.org%2F/1/0101019fa60d3716-9ebfc1af-930b-44b6-a45f-df967b0bbdd4-000000/Eo7cySbsj6wM9Ng8-ELc7iYoyxfA1HboVwktsmN6-II=452) Dear Friend, Wow, in all my years growing up and raising my family in this valley, I have never seen the devastation this year’s fire season has already presented. Every community I represent is impacted by the fires right now, and I am sending this newsletter to make sure all the contact and links for information continue to be spread to those looking for information. Since the fires started popping up after the the first lightening storm, I have engaged with federal, state and local agencies to make sure our communities are on the list for resources and services. This year our area has been one of the last to catch fire which resulted in a severe lack of ability to get equipment on the fires. While contractors are at the ready to head to the front lines, the protocol of the safety side of our agencies have not had the man-power to lead the divisions onto the front line. There is much I can dig into, and will, as it relates to this topic; but today I want to make sure you are aware of what is currently on the landscape. I am currently engaged every morning in the multiple cooperator’s meetings, which include agency and contract folks from US Forest Service, Bureau of Land Management, Oregon Department of Forestry and Oregon State Fire Marshal to our local Rangeland Fire Protection Associations, local Fire Chiefs, Sheriffs and all the array of additional folks that help organize the fight and many moving parts of the out of control fires. My goal is to ensure we have every possible resource on the ground to fight back. I pitch in where possible to coordinate evacuation of people, animals, or critical belongings (including storing snowcats). I listen to the issues of concern and have leaned directly on the Governor to find creative ways to get more middle management and get these fires out. I am proud of how our communities work together to help each other and I am grateful for the efforts of every person, paid and unpaid, which are serving our area. Please reach out to my office if you know of someone that needs help. 503-986-1459 or [Rep.VikkiBreeseIverson@oregonlegislature.gov](mailto:Rep.VikkiBreeseIverson@oregonlegislature.gov "Representative Vikki Breese Iverson"). Working Together, Vikki Breese Iverson |
* * *
---

*By subscribing to my e-mail updates, you are authorizing me to send regular e-mail updates from my office to your e-mail account.
#
# **Investing in Innovation That Saves Lives**

Senator Hughes joined Governor Shapiro and local leaders to celebrate [$125 million that will be invested into biotech and life science industry](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172142.172226.70&gen=1&mailing_linkid=18127) growth in Pennsylvania.
Senator Hughes fought for this money alongside Senate Democrats, House Democrats, and Governor Shapiro, despite opposition from Republicans.
The funding will help startups, fund programs that will provide opportunities for disadvantaged students to learn about the life sciences field, and bring new business to economically struggling areas.

* * *

**" Part of this funding will go to make sure that folks who historically did not get invested in, get invested in. Communities not too far away from here, blocks away from here, get the opportunity to allow their young people and their genius to be realized. That may be the most significant thing that happens as a result of this investment."**
**\- Senator Hughes**

* * *

[Senator Hughes spoke with the Philadelphia Tribune](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172142.172226.70&gen=1&mailing_linkid=18128) about the importance of making sure this new money reaches communities and business owners that have historically been left out.
[](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172142.172226.70&gen=1&mailing_linkid=18129)

[To learn more about this new money for innovation](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172142.172226.70&gen=1&mailing_linkid=18130) and other investments that were made in the state's new budget, [visit our website.](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172142.172226.70&gen=1&mailing_linkid=18126)

* * *

**Stay in Touch on Social Media**
If you haven't visited Senator Hughes' [**Facebook page**](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172142.172226.70&gen=1&mailing_linkid=18131), join the conversation by 'liking' the page and following our office on [**Instagram**](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172142.172226.70&gen=1&mailing_linkid=18133), [**TikTok**](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172142.172226.70&gen=1&mailing_linkid=18118), [**X**](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172142.172226.70&gen=1&mailing_linkid=18119), and [**Bluesky**](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172142.172226.70&gen=1&mailing_linkid=18121). We have lots of information available on these pages about community events and issues affecting our district.
If you have questions or concerns, send us an email at [**hughes@pasenate.com**](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172142.172226.70&gen=1&mailing_linkid=18122).

[ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
Derek,

I’ve had the honor of serving as
Pennsylvania’s 48th Governor for nearly four years now. And since I took
that oath on a frigid Tuesday in January, everyone here at Team Shapiro
has hit the ground running: We’ve cut taxes ten times, put money in folks’
pockets, invested in our schools, created jobs, and so much more.

Here’s another fact: Since Inauguration Day, we’ve received thousands of
grassroots donations — each and every one playing a pivotal role in what
we’ve accomplished together.

Trust me: In those high-stakes moments, the knowledge that thousands of
Pennsylvanians are behind our team is not lost on me.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/5015?t=1001&akid=156%2E245147%2EXxuEga ]With all that said, I’m sending you this email for a
reason, Derek. I
wanted to reach out and humbly ask: Will you make your first donation of the
year to our campaign to make sure our progress isn’t lost
on Election Day?

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/5015?t=1002&akid=156%2E245147%2EXxuEga ]Donate

Everything I’m working for is done in the service of hard-working
Pennsylvanians. I’m not beholden to a president or any special interest
group — and I never will be.

I’m beholden only to the good people of Pennsylvania.

But Derek, the
far-right is more than happy to allow some of the most extreme individuals
in the country to write and dictate their agenda in exchange for huge
piles of cash. But our campaign? We’re building this movement the
old-fashioned way: We’re spreading the word about everything we’re
fighting for — and hoping enough folks believe in that mission to chip in.

Pennsylvania fall to the far-right. Will you rush $25 or anything you can
ahead of our critical End-of-Month deadline on Friday night?

If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your

name: Doug Ollivant for Congress
subject: Built by Virginians. Backed by Virginians.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY OLLIVANT FOR CONGRESS
body:
Amanda Chase, Sheriff Giles & more stand with our all-Virginian, grassroots campaign.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/bAFaGpI4qjD?e=14c77a6723&c2id=09489c9156c428bed3a67a2822595ae0)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |

Dear Friends, Supporters, and Fellow Virginians,
I’m proud to share some important news.
We’ve received strong new endorsements from proven conservative leaders: former State Senator [**Amanda Chase, Jarome Bell, Sheriff Giles of King George County,** ](https://us.list-manage.com/88nYEZF8zat?e=14c77a6723&c2id=09489c9156c428bed3a67a2822595ae0)and****[**Daniel Cortez of Stafford County.**](https://us.list-manage.com/14wvQSsO27t?e=14c77a6723&c2id=09489c9156c428bed3a67a2822595ae0)
They understand the stakes in this race. And they are putting their names behind our campaign because they believe in the same things we do: **integrity, transparency, and results over empty talk.**
_**Amanda Chase**_ put it plainly: she _**supports a veteran who is backed by Virginians and who has been out working this district for months.**_ That is exactly the standard we should demand.
This campaign is primarily funded and supported by Virginians – not outside money. It is grassroots through and through. No special interests. Just ordinary people across the Commonwealth.
[**Every small donation matters. A $25 or $50 contribution from Prince William County, Spotsy, Culpeper, Stafford, Fredericksburg City, etc. is not just a number on a report but it is a declaration that this race belongs to the people who live here. Those dollars add up. They fund the yard signs, the mailers, the door-knocking, and the digital ads that let more Virginians hear a message free of special-interest spin. We only need neighbors who care enough to act.**](https://us.list-manage.com/dq2qRrVkfqh?e=14c77a6723&c2id=09489c9156c428bed3a67a2822595ae0)
Meanwhile, Yevgeny “Eugene” Vindman ran out of the 7th the first chance he got and declared his campaign for a different district the moment the maps looked inconvenient. Apparently, he still needs GPS just to find the rest of the district south and west of Prince William.

**I recently joined John Reid on The Reid Revolution to talk about this campaign and the future of Virginia’s 7th District.**[**You can listen here.**](https://us.list-manage.com/x9mt_f5UryT?e=14c77a6723&c2id=09489c9156c428bed3a67a2822595ae0)
That is why these endorsements matter. When conservatives who have actually fought for our principles choose to stand with a campaign built the right way by Virginians, for Virginians - it sends a clear signal.
Supporting conservatives is not about labels. It is about choosing people who will defend your values when it counts: defending our 2A rights, on spending, securing our borders, parental rights, and common sense. We need more of that in Washington, not less.
A quick reminder: **early voting is open**. You do not have to wait until August 4. Get to the polls, bring your friends and neighbors, and make sure your voice is heard.
Thank you for the continued support. We are building something real here and these endorsements show it.
Onward.
****

**Republican Candidate for U.S. Congress****Virginia’s 7th Congressional District**

[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP62/1/120031/images/eon%20header.png]
I want to tell you something that’s not easy to talk about...
A sitting Republican elected official recently tagged the Department of Homeland Security on social media and wrote:
"I would like to report a foreign occupier. Name: Unpronounceable. Country of origin: Tatooine." He was talking about me. The same official called for the mass deportation of Indian Americans.
I was born in New Delhi. I came to this country as a baby. I grew up in Peoria, Illinois. I went to public schools, got on food stamps for a time with my family, worked my way to Princeton and Harvard Law. I served in government. I got elected to Congress five times.
And someone still looked at all of that and saw a foreign occupier.
I'm telling you this not for sympathy. I'm telling you this because what happened to me is happening to communities all across this country right now, at a scale we have never seen before.
Trump and his MAGA allies have made it clear: if you weren't born here, if your name is hard to pronounce, if you look different or pray differently, you are not fully American in their eyes. They are using the machinery of the federal government to make that point, loudly and cruelly, every single day.
My father came here with nothing. He believed this country would be there for families like ours. It was. Because people fought for it.
That is exactly why I started Equal Opportunity Now.
We need leaders in office who will stand up for immigrant families and for every community that Trump has decided to make an enemy.
Those leaders exist. They are running for office right now. They need our support.
Will you chip in $25 or $50 today to help Equal Opportunity Now back the leaders who won't back down? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-eon]
CHIP IN TODAY TO DEFEAT MAGA EXTREMISM! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-eon]
It’s on us to stop the rising tide of MAGA Extremism. And with your help?
We’ll be unstoppable.
— Raja Krishnamoorthi

name: Mark Harris
subject: I stand with Sophie and Riley
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Mark Harris for Congress
body:
Courage like theirs deserves our support.

|
---
friend,

Women's spaces and women's sports should be for women, by women, and only for women.

That should be common sense.

Before I ever ran for office, I spent decades as a pastor — building up families, defending the values that hold our communities together.

That's the same conviction driving me today:_**protecting the people who can't always protect themselves, and standing up for what's right even when it's not politically convenient.**_

I'm grateful for athletes like Sophie Cunningham and Riley Gaines, who have had the courage to speak up for women and girls, often at real personal cost. They've set an example the rest of us should follow.

[](http://links.markharrisfornc.com/u/click?_t=7ae0368403444298b9ce39d60ff0dbbc&_m=e7ee96bb15b04ae9900e9948228629d3&_e=sTfKX45l9sqk4xLGxqXGnW95fZbKPd644Fdvf5tZdzwd9UbQjy5vojttOE8--uG4a6DICBQ6fx7kvfxWktm7iHu9D2M_ZrbofT0y27sEqYKuQLbY3JlNkLib63gyN01rmXL9SeBXujhyEv-7_uDpiuYE5GHd6m1ReIVY_VhPXcT5Vn4tmJZtjYuQYFaTZECBTp3z3BGDs_30zYEq4tgwJ6zPgnRRPfhZZJk8C_o5VTtwtokHU8lOdX53Z7zwAIixtIh8mknL9o3gXnzybSA5w5IlhnS1naAkjv4GI2Yu8jtMPQxfhdIKZ0qeXEPHlgtHMm9tE8cWUauOZEZTc030HAOSxOHU4KnaUqdmvCeasNJJ7OIb5ARcD11CKz-Al7AYfSr0F-ORzafpdeNeY1mTx8oHGsmg1Nvrjo_tp_XOWyzaXAGmNEfA0qSix2Pyx2UPciGnMvvLXeQsygFjapWyF0zKST2p1rLLIpVVLFW_edLO1Xg9ynJIsNSLMvJxLhn7zPXaHMoNr31dHvrt8gqubt5WF1QD59crrfHVDoDnfCw%3D)
Generations of women fought hard for the opportunities female athletes have today — scholarships, championships, a level playing field. _We are not going to let that be erased._

Republicans will keep doing our part to protect women's sports and defend those opportunities. But this fight takes resources, and it takes people willing to stand up when it matters.

name: Troy Jackson (via DNC HQ)
subject: How we win this race and defeat Susan Collins
body:
---
| [](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-jackson-split?amount=20&refcode=em_20260727_8260_fr&refcode2=8260_22930333_kJg8cG&akid=8260%2E22930333%2EkJg8cG)
---
Derek,
Growing up in Allagash and spending years working 80-hour weeks in the woods to make ends meet, I know firsthand what working Mainers need from our government.
And for 30 years, Susan Collins has failed us. Time and again, she has sold us out to Donald Trump and his MAGA agenda while pretending we’re too dumb to notice. **And I’m sick of it.**
My name is Troy Jackson. I’m a proud Mainer, father, and fifth-generation logger.
[**This weekend, I officially earned the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate. Now it’s time to defeat Susan Collins and her billionaire backers. So I’m asking you to split a donation between my campaign and the DNC to become a Founding Donor to my campaign right now and help us win one of the most important Senate races in the country and take back the Senate.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-jackson-split?refcode=em_20260727_8260_fr&amount=20&refcode2=8260_22930333_kJg8cG&akid=8260%2E22930333%2EkJg8cG)
**[SPLIT A CONTRIBUTION](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-jackson-split?refcode=em_20260727_8260_fr&amount=20&refcode2=8260_22930333_kJg8cG&akid=8260%2E22930333%2EkJg8cG)**
Derek, let me tell you a bit about what this race means to me.
When I was growing up, I was a poor kid in a town full of poor kids. My family relied on food assistance at times. I distinctly remember when I was 13 years old, we didn’t have heat or running water, and I heard my mother quietly crying to herself, wishing she could do more for us.
After high school, I became a logger like my dad, and his dad, and his dad before him. When a greedy landowner tried to screw my fellow loggers and me out of fair wages, I fought back. A whole bunch of politicians, including then-first-term Senator Susan Collins, promised to listen, but they left us high and dry — and I realized that _nothing would change_ unless there were working-class voices in power.
So I ran for the Maine legislature, where I served 20 years, including six years as the President of the Maine Senate. It’s been the honor of my life to fight for working people.
I drove hours each way between the North Woods and the State Capitol, because that's what the job required. I won those elections in a district that went for Trump by nearly 20 points, because up here, people care less about a label and more about whether you give a damn about their family.
Derek, I’m building this campaign the right way. With grassroots support from folks like you. I’m not running to impress the billionaires or the corporate class. I’m running for the mom who’s worried about how she’ll fill her gas tank this week. I’m running for the kid whose whole life will be determined by the quality of his education. I’m running to ensure every working family in Maine has the government they deserve.
[**If you believe in this fight and our movement, I’m humbly asking you to split a donation between my campaign and the DNC today to help us reach our fundraising goal and take on the GOP’s millions in Maine and beyond. Even $5 makes a difference >>**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-jackson-split?refcode=em_20260727_8260_fr&amount=20&refcode2=8260_22930333_kJg8cG&akid=8260%2E22930333%2EkJg8cG)

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

On August 19, 2004, Google went public.

If you were watching CNBC that morning, you saw a historic moment. You saw the share price open at $85, you saw a generation of new tech millionaires take the stage, and you saw the trading floor erupt.

You almost certainly weren't one of those millionaires.

That's because IPO shares — the ones priced before the bell rings — are reserved for institutional buyers, accredited investors, and people with connections in Silicon Valley. Everyone else trades the after-market, after the easy money is gone.

Facebook in 2012. Uber in 2019. Airbnb in 2020. Same pattern. Same outcome.

The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | On August 19, 2004, Google went public. If you were watching CNBC that morning, you saw a historic moment. You saw the share price open at $85, you saw a generation of new tech millionaires take the stage, and you saw the trading floor erupt. You almost certainly weren't one of those millionaires. That's because IPO shares — the ones priced before the bell rings — are reserved for institutional buyers, accredited investors, and people with connections in Silicon Valley. Everyone else trades the after-market, after the easy money is gone. Facebook in 2012. Uber in 2019. Airbnb in 2020. Same pattern. Same outcome. There is now an AI startup the Wall Street Journal calls "the front-runner in the race for artificial-intelligence supremacy." Initial SEC paperwork is filed. Outside counsel has been retained. Bloomberg calls the IPO "imminent." This time, there is a way in before the bell. Jeff Brown has identified a publicly traded company — available in any brokerage account, for less than $50 — that already holds billions in shares of this startup. You can take a position today, ahead of the people who couldn't. |

body:
Billionaire Rick Jackson spent $120 million to win the Republican nomination for Governor.
I'm writing to ask for $3.
No, that's not a typo.
Rick Jackson says he’s going to be "President Trump's favorite governor,” so we need all hands on deck. Will you split a donation of $3 or more between my campaign and Dr. Jasmine Clark to help us flip Georgia blue? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-klb]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-klb]
Look, after spending $120 million trying to buy this election, Jackson is already preparing to spend millions more to buy the Governor's Mansion.
He just reserved $87 million worth of TV commercials for the fall.
So you might be thinking – $3 isn't very much money. How can we stand up to a billionaire with $3?
That's the point.
This campaign isn’t powered by billionaires. It's powered by thousands of people chipping in what they can because they believe Georgia deserves a governor who will fight for them.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-klb [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-klb]
And when thousands of people chip in just a few dollars, we can build something powerful.
Your $3 helps us organize in communities across the state.
Your $3 helps us reach voters before Rick Jackson's attack ads do.
Your $3 sends a message that Georgia belongs to its people—not the wealthy politicians trying to buy it.
If everyone reading this email gave just $3, we'd raise the resources we need to compete with Rick Jackson's fortune.
So please: Will you make a contribution of $3 (or more, if you can!) to help defeat Rick Jackson and elect the first Democratic Governor of Georgia this century? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-klb]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-klb]
From the bottom of my heart: Thank you.
—Keisha Lance Bottoms

subject: Hegseth’s extreme pastor is now “mainstream”

Friends [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50] , do you remember this guy? NPR just published a new interview with Pete Hegseth’s personal spiritual leader — the extremely fringe, right-wing pastor Doug Wilson. And this headline has all the alarm bells ringing:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25]
Mainstream. That’s the word religion and history scholars are using to describe how Wilson’s teachings have moved from the fringes of our society to the mainstream, now that Donald Trump’s administration is filled with Christian nationalists.
In case you need a refresher on who this guy is: He’s made disturbing and shameful claims defending slavery and saying it wasn’t that bad . He thinks we should criminalize homosexuality. He said God created women “to make the sandwiches” and that wives should submit to their husbands. And he believes the 19th Amendment should be repealed — because granting women the right to vote was a “bad idea.”
To be extremely clear: My role in society isn’t to submit to a man. It’s to be a Member of Congress. And a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee and Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Africa. And a member of the House Armed Services Committee. And to serve as the Parliamentarian in the House Democratic Caucus, making me one of the youngest members of Democratic House leadership.
Get the picture, pastor?
But in case there was any doubt about Wilson’s vision for our country, he’s made it clear in the NPR interview that his full focus is on banning abortion nationwide, overturning marriage equality, and gradually turning the United States into a Christian theocracy — where religion controls our government and politics, in direct violation of our Constitution. Under his vision, non-Christians wouldn’t be able to hold public office.
This is despicable.
We can’t be shocked anymore by this administration, but we can stay outraged — and channel that anger into getting these racist, sexist, homophobic, egotistical losers out of power so they stop infecting our country with their rot and putting us on the fast-track to white nationalism and authoritarianism.
That’s my mission, and I know we can do it if we roll up our sleeves and get to work. I’m all in on this — my team and I are laser-focused on retaking a Democratic House majority, working to support Democratic challengers and incumbents, and of course winning my own re-election. | | **Anthropic's $1.5 Billion Copyright Settlement Is Final. The Legal Line Is Not 'AI Training Is Illegal' — It Is How the Training Library Was Acquired.**
---
| | U.S. District Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín granted final approval on July 20 to Anthropic's $1.5 billion class-action settlement with authors and publishers over books obtained from pirate libraries. The settlement covers 482,460 eligible works and is expected to provide roughly $3,000 per work before deductions and allocation among rightsholders. Claims were submitted for 440,490 works — 91.3% of the eligible list — giving the agreement an unusually high participation rate and making it the largest known copyright recovery by total value.
---
| | The risk lesson is narrower and more useful than the headline: an earlier ruling treated training on lawfully acquired books as fair use in the circumstances before that court, while the separate acquisition and retention of pirated copies remained legally exposed. The settlement is not a universal declaration that AI training is unlawful, nor is it a blanket license for future datasets. For model developers, data provenance is now a balance-sheet control: source records, license terms, dataset chain of custody, deletion obligations, model lineage and reserve estimates need the same governance as other material intellectual-property risks. For publishers and authors, the agreement strengthens the commercial case for explicit licensing, audit rights and traceable compensation mechanisms.
---
| | Sources: AP News — Final approval of the $1.5 billion Anthropic settlement; approximately $3,000 per covered work; U.S. District Court via Justia — Order granting final settlement approval and judgment, July 20, 2026; Authors Guild — 440,490 of 482,460 eligible works claimed, a 91.3% participation rate

body:

| | | | | | We had Nick Shirley on this weekend — the 24-year-old who exposed those Minnesota daycares pulling in millions with no children inside. California just passed a bill going after him for exposing the fraud instead of the people committing it. [It’s unreal.](https://us.list-manage.com/PtSnFzrTpUy?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)

Then there's KRQE ending 72 years with CBS. Mark worked in that building a long time, and we don't think this goes the way they think it's going to.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/3R9Je7U7zAP?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| |
**🔥 THE BILL WITH HIS NAME ON IT**
Nick Shirley can't go to a gas station without being recognized anymore, and he films with security now. That's what exposing fraud gets you.
He walked us through what California's bill actually does and why he doesn't think the timing is an accident. The woman who wrote it is married to the Attorney General, which is a detail worth sitting with.
Then he told us about Cuba. A two-star general showed up at his hotel at four in the morning, and he was on foot in the streets of Havana by five. We're not going to spoil how he got out.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/15AOd6vV1L9?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |
**🚨 18,000 NEW MEXICANS OFF SNAP — AND THE NUMBER NOBODY PRINTS**
More than 10,000 of them are children, and that's what every headline led with.
Here's the one buried at the bottom. **New Mexico's error rate is 16.8%,** and if the state doesn't get it under 6% by October of 2027, we owe at least $150 million.
Deb Haaland put out a statement about all of it. Read it closely and tell us what's missing.

**📺 CHANNEL 13 GOES FULL-TIME FOX ON AUGUST 1**
CBS moves to a KOAT subchannel, which isn't the same thing as KOAT picking up a second station, and that difference matters more than anyone's letting on.
Mark started the Fox newscast in this market in 2006, so he has a good idea what Nexstar was looking at — and what they missed about New Mexico specifically.
**Nobody's talking yet about where the political ad money goes now, and it lands right in the middle of the governor's race.

****🏛️ NEW MEXICO IS SUDDENLY THE 4TH PRIMARY IN THE COUNTRY**
February 15, 2028. Not June, where we've always been parked and nobody ever came. PLUS: Senator Tim Sheehy's speech on the Senate floor about Iran, the AP's story on Nepal after the USAID cuts, and a USA Today columnist who compared Caitlin Clark drawing a foul to the lynching of Emmett Till. USA Today is standing behind it.

Effects from the earthquake were felt throughout the rural region and as far as southern Oklahoma and New Mexico.

On social media, Spearman residents said the earthquake shook homes. Some in Oklahoma City, nearly 250 miles away, reported feeling the effects of the earthquake.

**“Texas reports biggest drop in crime rate in five years”** via [The Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/udc5KaCmYGNsoKG7SJlIvTsqSzo9pMb086kBIjqXowCUlpHZ1ZE80ldW9hJf%0A5eBgAy4fS8gf0dKVLgJpeTACdvF5mkyHRFJqHK6AwVgh%2BBT%2B6%2Fxw2tg0Fm0U%0AiwaX00ngKMRCTXfyA45VW52yyMDeXcc1EBgY9trhcX%2F3iqOkP20bnHo733ja%0AI8rQnA9XVnVVJyxymPVsuWnGkX3KW%2BW7RA%3D%3D%0A/cb428a8d45065877)‘s **Berenice Garcia** — In 2019, a historic theater’s marquee in McAllen’s downtown district once lauded, “Welcome to McAllen, 7th Safest city in America.”

The theater placed the message front and center ahead of a visit from President **Donald Trump** during his first term in office, using it to dispute the narrative at the time that the border was a dangerous place. The ranking itself came from a 2015 study by Smart Asset, a financial technology website.

Now, 10 years after that report, McAllen is highlighting its crime rate again — this time, celebrating its lowest crime levels in 40 years.

Crime in Texas has been decreasing since 2023, according to Uniform Crime Reporting Data released by the Texas Department of Public Safety. In the last five years, crime in Texas peaked in 2022 — with a rate of 2,830.14 per 100,000 people — before trending downward. Between 2022 and 2023, the state’s crime rate decreased by 3.3%, and between 2023 and 2024, the crime rate dropped another 8.2%. The West Texas school trustees voted unanimously Tuesday to proceed with a lawsuit against Education Commissioner **Mike Morath** and state leaders, arguing that funding restrictions imposed by the Legislature prohibit them from raising and spending money to meet the needs of their students.

“We can sit here on this stage, and we can complain about it,” Midland ISD Board President **Josh Guinn** said before the vote. But nothing changes, Guinn added, “until you have four people — elected school board members — in the state of Texas say, ‘Enough’s enough. You’re going to stop stealing our community’s money.’”

Guinn said in an interview that he expected the district to file the lawsuit by 5 p.m. Wednesday but could not yet confirm whether it occurred. Last week, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration ordered the companies to explain by the end of July how they will keep their vehicles from entering emergency scenes, blocking responders or failing to recognize flashing lights and other hazards.

Austin has seen such incidents firsthand. In one high-profile case, first responders heading to a March 1 mass shooting downtown faced an unexpected obstacle: self-driving robotaxis. The shooting left three people dead and the gunman was fatally shot by police. Fifteen others were injured. Effects from the earthquake were felt throughout the rural region and as far as southern Oklahoma and New Mexico. According to the U.S. Geological Survey, the earthquake occurred at 5:21 a.m. nearly 24 miles south-southeast of Spearman near the top of the Texas-Oklahoma border. On social media, Spearman residents said the earthquake shook homes. Some in Oklahoma City, nearly 250 miles away, reported feeling the effects of the earthquake. A.J. Harrel , a meteorologist with the National Weather Service in Amarillo, said the earthquake originated from northwest Roberts County, nearly 50 miles south of Spearman. Harrel said Thursday’s earthquake was stronger than what they typically see in the region. ( ) “Texas reports biggest drop in crime rate in five years” via ‘s Berenice Garcia — In 2019, a historic theater’s marquee in McAllen’s downtown district once lauded, “Welcome to McAllen, 7th Safest city in America.” The theater placed the message front and center ahead of a visit from President Donald Trump during his first term in office, using it to dispute the narrative at the time that the border was a dangerous place. The ranking itself came from a 2015 study by Smart Asset, a financial technology website. Now, 10 years after that report, McAllen is highlighting its crime rate again — this time, celebrating its lowest crime levels in 40 years. Crime in Texas has been decreasing since 2023, according to Uniform Crime Reporting Data released by the Texas Department of Public Safety. In the last five years, crime in Texas peaked in 2022 — with a rate of 2,830.14 per 100,000 people — before trending downward. Williams transports about a third of the nation’s natural gas, he said, and it recently expanded into the power generation business. ( ) “Dallas security company Brinks Home hit by cyberattack, blackmail attempt” via ‘ Trevor Bach – Brinks Home, a Dallas-based home security company, was hit by a cyberattack that infiltrated the company’s IT systems, the company said Wednesday. Brinks Home did not disclose the identity of the attacker but also implied the company was being blackmailed. “The party responsible for this situation has threatened to release information it claims to have taken,” Brinks Home wrote in an update published on its website. “We are aware that such material may be posted publicly.” It was unclear exactly what information may have been exposed to the breach, but in a statement to The Dallas Morning News the company emphasized that it was working “as quickly as possible to determine the full scope of what occurred” and that its systems are secure. ( ) “Austin developers planning 1,736-acre community in Hill Country” via ‘ Richard Webner – Two developers from Austin are teaming up to build a 1,736-acre master-planned community on vacant land east of Interstate 35 in Hays County — adding thousands of homes in a region already undergoing rapid growth. Known as the Ridge, the community will feature more than 6,200 single-family home sites, along with a multifamily development, according to the website of one of the developers, Wilson Capital. It will sit to the west of Texas 21 and Rohde Road, about 4 miles west of Kyle. Sites have been reserved for elementary, middle and high schools, according to a map on Wilson Capital’s website. To give a sense of scale, the community will be about half the size of San Antonio’s 3,500-acre downtown. Wilson Capital is partnering with Carlton Capital Investments on the community, which is expected to cost $375 million to build, said Taylor Wilson , the president of Wilson Capital. They expect to begin construction this year, with the first phase taking 10 months, Taylor Wilson said. The development team has entitlements lined up for the required utilities, he said. ( ) “Inside the building boom reshaping Fort Worth’s Cultural District” via ‘s Harrison Mantas – Fort Worth’s Cultural District is growing up. Literally. Construction cranes are bringing office towers to an area once dotted with auto body shops, small storefronts, and single family homes. The area once known for its popular bars and nightclubs is slated to become a place where people live and work rather than just play. Apartment buildings, office buildings, hotels, stores and restaurants are popping up in the district. Nebraska-based Goldenrod Companies is in the midst of building two mixed-use towers near the Artisan Circle development along West Seventh Street. “I can’t be more bullish on this neighborhood right here,” former Goldenrod executive John Zogg said during an October 2023 meeting on the future of the Fort Worth Community Arts Center. ( ) | TRUMP ADMINISTRATION “President Trump approves Texas’ major disaster declaration” via – President Donald Trump has approved Texas’ major disaster declaration, allowing the state to receive federal disaster assistance. The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) announced the approval Saturday, just one day after Texas Gov. Greg Abbott signed the declaration. “The President’s action authorizes FEMA to coordinate all federal disaster relief efforts to alleviate the hardship and suffering caused by the emergency on the local population, and to provide appropriate assistance to save lives, to protect property, public health and safety and to lessen or avert the threat of a catastrophe,” a news release from FEMA said. The federal aid will be available for the 28 counties hit hardest by the heavy rains and flooding over the past week, including Uvalde, Kerr and Kendall counties. Abbott said on Friday that more counties could be added depending on the need. Neuralink is a neurotechnology company founded by Elon Musk in 2016 that develops implantable brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) pictured. Its core device, the coin-sized N1 "Link," is surgically placed under the skull with ultra-thin flexible electrode threads that record neural activity and wirelessly transmit it to external devices, allowing users to control computers, phones, or robotic limbs purely with their thoughts. Currently in human trials (with over 20 participants as of early 2026), it primarily helps people with severe paralysis or ALS regain digital independence--enabling cursor control, typing, gaming, and emerging speech decoding. Looking ahead, Neuralink aims to expand into restoring vision (via its Blindsight project), hearing, and speech; treat conditions like Parkinson's; scale to high-volume automated surgeries; and ultimately create a high-bandwidth bidirectional interface that could enable seamless human-AI symbiosis and cognitive enhancement for healthy users.

## ****Wildfires in Europe Force 300,000 to Flee
Wildfires tearing across France and Spain [have forced](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO5CAQRL_GzmzhNjOYgOASZ3PphVYbmjEnDBYww87fr9hf2KTVUpVeqerfY3ug8y48_-JJqti4BarZUymUNnqleBEG6xIZlzEXSrnZN2BwH5gYYNkMOv_ZeG-UJQKae1KTWG4wc36D_lAgp5kMSb7fmbZcCJQL03yXtEyST6Z3qtGYgGViIECO0jKxMy4WwUBoxI4zMq7ENP6PLpSDrP_EN6VRx7P36ijlyt38p4O1g7XWOuqw6yZ2sDZ0BysT7W-nOm9anzzkC10YbMKgadhjMoSvr-EgLBXfNB7l9H1S5qrOe5fvouPseaLzP7HlV1u9FXwHAAD__xkXfQI) more than 300,000 people from their homes, triggering the largest peacetime evacuation in French history since World War II. The blaze near Bordeaux has burned an area four times the size of Paris in under a week and spawned a rare "fire thunderstorm," a towering cloud that generates its own winds and lightning capable of igniting new fires. [See the maps here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uGyEQhZ-G7bDwgA0uKBwl2zlNipSruTB4SVhYAdfIbx9tpDxB2vk5Ot_387E8MKaYn99xI9tDWTKNlqh3qgt91rIT5hAr-diwdartOF9AwJULzcEsHmN6L2ryNhAByYnsWZsLSKUuMK1WKen81SGQDP58ufibhEDGO6fOGMxtivZIExrMWYCG2-kWhP4QShstQDtEpgT52Es9_Sox95VCepcX1ZMr25Ts2vvemLwzmBnMY4zT1vKxYzBT5p_tmBL2lSqD-UmZKiYGs6cXto495if_R8pHTP7AbTxmvuHeOGbP1zJ4X-nNK_EPOh46ut-JPIMZK7_fwTze3wyTc3HRM_n1y2GURvtBdZ-q9fuIKcV21UyJ54Yx_e3e_0v4y8KfAAAA__9DOpdK). Spain has declared a national emergency as crews battle the largest fire in the Madrid region's history. A 78-year-old man [was killed](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDFuhDAQRU8DnZGZNRgKF2noNm1KNNjjZSIvRrazaG8fOVdIN9Ib_a_3v-7rHTnw8fjEJ5ni43rQlQOVQmmlnxRPwsNzIscZc6GU6_sKEkYhtYBpdcjhvarWGU8EdGvJ9Hoa4KbUAO1u5mGDUYLD3slpcLMcEaR14Hql3WC3lk1NkxqmXoKGuZu91JtUetIStEVslCTHJabuO_JRdvLhHV-UOhufbTB7KWdubh8NLA0s13V1dsvVovIGlnpWwMFVkSx8wsOSyCfyIXbCIi58kfAxkcVcGljaZNx5cQicR90o-Xgih7-68q-NXgZ-AwAA__-I1Xw7) near Valencia, and two firefighters died near Bordeaux. Chilling CCTV captured flames racing from distant mountains to a home's doorstep in just eight minutes. [See the footage here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDFuhDAQRU8DnZF3MJgtXKSh27QpkcHjZRJjI3sWtLePyBXSP339974e08NSoPj8tBsa9mmKeJaAzJgnfOW0o42eMjoqtjDmcuETSOiF1AKGyVkK70nVznhEwLZGc9NDB61SHdSrAd_NvXay88vcDuB61Q0etWp7uFmUS03mWpMahpsEDffm7qWepdKDlqAXaysl0RGn3HwniryiD-90YG6WtNXBrMx7qdqPCsYKxvM8G4oOd4wOIzdLal4_FYx8VDBebhdDwV1ORZTdUhSbdZmcWBY-hE-J7RPFQQ6TmFsJAHJoVt5CnY3bTwqBSq8rJZ-bpfB3gv9V7jDwGwAA__9GyINJ). A fourth heat wave arrives midweek, with temperatures near 104 degrees.
## ****Sen. Rand Paul Releases Fauci Diary Details
Newly released diary entries from Dr. Anthony Fauci show he privately estimated COVID-19's case fatality rate at 0.2–0.3% in February 2020, but told Congress weeks later the mortality rate was around 1%, or [10 times more lethal](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGupDAQRE8DmUemMRgCB5uQ_U03RI3dDL0yGNk9w5_br9gr_LieSlXvz9f8hRz5eP7GnZysaT7oKpFEKM_0yukkPFbOFLhgEcrlxmfQ0CttFQxzQI6f2dTBrURAbU2usUMHrTEd1Jsbh7YjswAuPerGoum6Yex98AsGu3hds7vbtIWh0WBhfIyrtos2drAarEesjKbAkvLjb-JDNlrjJ70pP3za6-g2kbNU7a8Kpgqm67oea_q-X9x5BdOZIgv7UsFE32cqFNSKL88qMOaPKlu6iqIivKNQUD69OahmVIFQNpVRSO0vv6mYLspKUryZ45mplDq7cF4cI5feVkY_d-T4f5b8yOXbwb8AAAD__ydcjDE) than the seasonal flu. Sen. Rand Paul, a longtime critic of Fauci's pandemic performance, released the [1,141-page diary](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOszAQBOCnsTuiZcEYChd_Q5e_vRIZvI73ZHBkO4l4-xP3ClfP6JNmvu7L3XLk4_Hf7mSqT8tBnxKpVsoLvXJ6kj08Z3JcbKmUy1VfEHBoQDc4Ls5yPJdeOuOJkDpJptWjwq7vFcpglN9WslPbuk3p1Y24dgCkp037dRhASTaXBhrHFlDjdJs86BV6PWpAvVkreiDHNeXbd-KjBvLxTG_Kty3tMppQ67OI7p_AWeBcAwWO8coEziHtdA0SOKtpQmhV4-1r48axzWdDR81MpckUyRZyAmeZjXt-OEYugxY9PHbLv5qsf7rnbfAnAAD__9hLeVw) ahead of Fauci's subpoenaed Senate testimony Wednesday. Paul chairs the committee investigating the federal COVID response and origins of the virus. The entries also reveal [a striking fixation on fame](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO3CAQBuCnwR0rdpZdcEGRxt2lTWmNzXA7EQYLsC_O00fkFa77pRl9mvl_fcwfyJHT50_cyLWQ50RfNVJrVGY6St4JU-BCnivWRqX29RkUvKQyEuzskeM168G7QAT0GMjdjX3CQ-snDG83egvry46vgIsZrQFtvLo_F9B20YrswK5ryoC9KzAw3sagzKK0sUaBWRGFVuS55XL7nTm1N4V45ZPKbc3bEN27tb2Kxw8Bk4ApXXuurY8ETB0WMCnTc09Hlf0_AZMvMuCxcpUL_8VSSAbcSAb-g41zkljlmk_20hO2d5VbPlIjLwudhJG85NSpeMlCkbCSl56xMHV8KM7vXxwj15cRWn1uyPH_ue1bHZ8O_gUAAP__Q9aQ9g). As U.S. deaths climbed into the tens of thousands, Fauci pasted flattering headlines into his journal and wrote it was "not hyperbole" to call himself the most famous person in the country.
## Sailor Survives a Month Adrift in Pacific
A California sailor stranded in the Pacific for over a month [was rescued](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGynDAMQE9jOu8ILYuhcJGG7qdNyQiQQRlj79j-ePb2GZIjpFPxRk9Pv77mLxIvYf9JJ9vi4hy4Zs-lcJr5O8U3U3CSeJNMuXDKNz4jYK_BaBzmjcR_5q7ZrGNGfjZsWzO88Nl1L2wOu7QEpqVx6bcR1lfv-hYBeF0WgCfB0oi9t4HBoQU0OD5GB2aBzgwG0KxEqgPepMT0-B0llIOd_8SL02ONZ-PtUco7q-cPhZPCqdb6OKiSyB0SYr0phdPtUDiBueeXwilHH_Vdo_cYWNcUw65X8uJiCkL6pKDzd7rk4qzPGMqhM5PekrgiYdf_JAqnJtntXcV7yb1RHewnif97W_mvh14W_wQAAP__4vKLHQ) by a passing container ship after drifting hundreds of miles off course toward Hawaii. Kai Sato, 39, left Catalina Island on June 7, attempting his first solo Pacific crossing. Two weeks in, [his mast snapped](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAQRL8GOiOzGOwrXKShu7Qp0R5eHxsZG9nOofv7iPxC2jej0cx83Zc7cuD4_MSdbPVpiXSWQLVSXugnp4Mwes7kuGCplMtlX0DCJKQWYBaHHN6Lap31REBDS7bXZoRBqRHazZpR33pEcEZLMz1Ijkq5aQJHnvoH-ZbtlSY1mF6Chlt381I_pNJGS9ArYqMkOa4pd9-JY93Ih3d6Ue7WtLfBbrUepRk-GpgbmM_z7N64pXSpDczXnAunHFwDM-bKa6AL7RhFqRmjIyf2FOsmDlzZ8yrSShhFr8ahH0Gpbqt7aLN1x8khcJl0o-RzRw5_Feq_fntZ-A0AAP__EQiCDA), his fuel ran out, and his phone, his only way to call for help, died. Sato lived on oatmeal, plus fish and squid that landed on deck, and licked condensation off plastic bags stretched over buckets of seawater. [See photos here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO6yAQRb8Gd0R44hhSULzGXV67pTU2QzwrDBYQR_n7FfsL213NjI7m3K_H_EAOHJ__cSdbfZojvUugWinP9MrpIIyeMzkuWCrl0s5nUDBKpSWY2SGHzzx0znoioGtHttfmBtdhuEG3WfRmpX4EGkfv0SD4pb8vaBYyy6hvumPbaEqD6RVouF_uXulFDdpoBXpFFIMixzXly3fiWDfy4ZNOypc17V2wW61HEdd_AiYBU_wcqdS2EjA1sIBJ6ZZbehXZ_ARMKwb2KUdGuWOUpWaMjpxMUTbFJWGV5ZVPPqnIPcW6yTYhFDB12brjzSFwGbUY1HNHDr_f1D9VeFr4CQAA__-f7oXf). A makeshift rig he built from PVC pipes and kayak paddles took nearly a month to carry him back to the shipping lane, where [a cargo crew](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOszAQBOCngc5oWZzYFC7-Jl3-9kq0gXXYi8GR7cTK25-4V7j-04xmvq7TlSTIfv9PG7vi47RzzYFL4TTxK8Un0-4l8SKZcuGUDz4h4FmBUWinhSR8Jt0uzjMjDy273tgTDlqfsF2dHwBHvVi-mRMZO3jQFvE2Gw_z2CO34o40MGh7QINjN3owN9DGGkAzEzUaeJESU_cdZS8r-_CJb07dHLc2uLWUZ26Gfw1eGrzUWrtjQmV-HKDBy0xBfEy7kNpoVw8SlalEFWIuKjOplSqJqMR5frHqEfUIZ2yTW55VQpB8No2G-0YSfjvLn456O_wJAAD__5RKfPc) pulled him aboard. Next up, he says: the Philippines.

## Patrick Expands Religious Liberty Agenda
Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick issued [seven new interim charges](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD3ypCAQxU-jGRa0IhoQbGI2m25otdIquygW9Iwzt99yrvDPXvDqffz-PMYH-uCP9TfuZPm9xPGgKwdipnTLjZDTM1BeYspnTJz_ximPIKEV0gjoRoc-fMamdHaSrlclWWU6DXWrtSo3i06bzqlZw0TgULUw6xpcj8o4mjpZenuHSQOdUhKgqVRvjFau6bul1oukopHkPMdU8UZMb8xL-MQXpWqOexnsxnzmov5VwFDAcF1XtcQ3tFt8Zo7HbSpguF8VMDg8xImc_PxPJAp-9fGZRfATJf6IOe67ZyYSuNLhUHzbRKYDmcpk3Xn5EHxuTdHIdUcfvhP4Z-BeFv4HAAD__6wKhg8) to the Texas Senate on Monday, three of them aimed at its newly formed Religious Liberty Committee. The committee will [compare Texas and federal religious protections](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGPnDAQhX8NdF6ZwcZQUKShu7Qp0aw9Bue8GNmzy92_j7xp0qcZPek9fdI3vz7WDwwxHNtPfNDMXz6tB10lEjPlGndCzs9IxadczpS5_E73soKEQUgjYFwdhvi9qtbNd-mmrqW5M6OGftC6a_fZOWl7aTyQNmrA0SpQ_u7Jge7Ro27DXGHSwNh1EkDduskY3Tk1jb7XXlKjJLnAKd94J6YvLD5-pxflm02PNs4781ma_kcDSwPLdV23z9eTatnAgpmDjdTAUr0aWM4UAwdb45slIm2hRORnriuHhziRc7Cf4m9f6ECmf2fioEvYHfNGFQPDJFD1Cow0Qimqx2iBozRCjsMkLfm77nybZ3deIcZQBtMouT0wxLcD_9_nXzP8CQAA__8uo5gd), study ways to educate Texans about their religious rights, and monitor new laws requiring Ten Commandments displays in classrooms and allowing prayer periods in public schools. "_Come January, the Senate and I will advance the priorities of Texas' conservative majority_ ," Patrick [said](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkMGOpCAURb8GdxJAEF2wqExiMoua7SwNJQ-lg2LglVb9fcdK_0HvTl5O3r25_-_j3YYYtvmfXcHgy6dxg7NEQIR84QIW8zNC8SmXPWUsX-lRRsFEWzNdi250NsT3KCtnHsz1vALDdadE0yrFq8X0jWzbh5q0s1or3nCpVddq1U9CeiV9Fcz1jGnRcc6EkJT3l-hk3_lGeQZEMnABU6a4AMLLFh_f6YBMp7RW0SyIeyHNjYiBiOE8TxpxTgf9qHROx3Xd6yltCBsSMTz3mKwrRAxXMhED0z9c35wLGNJmY_13Q8hhrf8sNs9Q6O58lY3bzxBjKK0mks2rDfHTAn-33WHEdwAAAP__IwCCTw). The charges follow his tenure as chair of President Trump's federal Religious Liberty Commission. The classroom displays remain contested: a divided Fifth Circuit [upheld the law in April](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2SpTAMhE9jMlO2bP4CB5uQzaYbUgKJh7cMZm0zzNx-i3eFyVSS-qvu_vMxfaAP_nj9xp1d-VrjdPCdA5fC6Rk3xpKuwHmNKZ8xlfw3znkCBa1UnYR-IvThe7IVuVnRoCt2uusbMG3T6GpzYKw1prN2IDJEmhmbHnEBTcSzaSvvHpjqoNdaAdhaD13XaLJDv5pmVSysYvIlprpsXPgL8xq-4yeneol7FdxWypmF-SVgFDDe910vc35SPHcB41siYHxWAsaViRMGiefJGLJc4pWKvM4tBsry_SwD3jLxv8snf7xk4UMucd_xoJ2PkqU_5BIw5xTj_iCr5Oi8fQg-t52w6rWjD2935Wedfjr4HwAA__9Or4_6), and the multifaith families who sued say they'll ask the Supreme Court to reverse it.
## Midland Father Charged in Toddler's Death
A Midland father has been charged with capital murder after police say his 2-year-old daughter [died Sunday inside a locked car](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL_O3CAQxJ8Gd5xg_Qe7oEjj7kub0lqb5SDBxoK983dvHzmvkGb0K0Yzo_n1tXxhTPF4_sSdLH_7vBx01UTMVG4MhFxeiarPpZ65cP2d17qAgkEqI2FcHMb0WbrG2VW5STdktRl7aIe-102wsG6AHlsE8Gr0I6xq6NQ6GT1tehp9E-0dpgyMWiuA7qEnY3rtumn0be8ViU6Ri5zLgwMxfWP16ZPfVB5b3ptkA_NZRftDwCxgvq7r4WOpjIkKm9sjYL4rBMzK3HyLRw5U5BawPMnJK3KQG56RMcn9VRwViZ6pSJAfwiJzctLn1-GkI3Qy5e0POfmmELdEco8u4eEEzE2x7rxiSrEORnTquWNM_4by_937tvA3AAD__74aj-c) parked outside their home. Relatives told police they went to check on Lorenzo Rodriguez, 25, and his daughter after he'd been drinking the night before. When knocking brought no answer, they pulled out a window air-conditioning unit and climbed inside. They found Rodriguez asleep and learned he had been unconscious since about 11 a.m. The girl wasn't inside. Family members found her in a parked Kia, broke a window, and [rushed her to Midland Memorial Hospital](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGS6yAQRE8jZaMChAQKCH6izD_dUIXFYNhFRgVjy779lnyFzV7wZqq7vy7LxcYU77f_dkNDL5-XOx41IRGWEwNaKo-E1edS91yofudrXQQTIzAFQi_OxvReZOvMlbmJt2i40oPox2HgbTATimlSQ7_KHrV2Ei1Kb6XWI5MeuWyjOZ8xJTTnTAjZ8UmpgTs5ad8PnmEjGbpIuXQUkPBlq0_v_MTSrXlrkwlEe236f42YGzEfx9H5_JJnjVNoxHxiI-bPKXhLAQuswZYbOljtHskm2B7FYQHrCQsIeKMtkJMDF7FCyuvPxy1whJgQAkJNuFNbjNuPmFKso2oku202pk8s-tuYTyN-AwAA__94hYwI), where she died. Police estimate the toddler spent [about nine hours in the vehicle](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2SozAQhJ9GZHJJw48gUHAJmS-9kBrQALoaJJckY_vtt9hgX2CzDrq6vv7-3ac7evZh-4sH2fJe4xTolZlKoXTFnbCkJ1NeY8qPmEr-H-c8gYJOKiOhnxx6_kxN5eys3KArstr0LdRd2-pqtwqbpdW1GmbXzdgoWKDrOm2GmgYkjZW315gy0GutAJqbHoxptWuGfq3bVZFoFDlfYrqVnQq9Ma_8iSel2xKPiu1eyiOL-o-AUcCYMWDYiCP7k66GgPG6JGBckj9IwPgDbwSMh3eMwckDg1x2TBs5eTyToyRxLZQkE54-bLJE55iSPGn3C1OVrHu8PLPPnRGN2g70_E1UfufxtPAVAAD__15KiEU). Rodriguez was arrested after officers responded at 7:56 p.m.
## Mandatory Heat Rules Start Aug. 1
Every Texas high school must follow [mandatory heat-safety rules](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL3ypCAQxJ9GM7Zg_EADgkvM_pdeaLEyCFfobMG4rm9_5b7CZR10d_Wv__zMPzamuK-_7YaGP57mHc-SkBnzLQNazkfC4imXF2Uuf-lZZpDQC6kFDLOzMV1zWzvzlG5UNRqlhw6avutUHYxcpF7UiOh12z1HB1L24NAP2HRWD7KO5i6TGgalJED7UKPWnXLtOPim8xKrVqKLTPnBARk_tvh00RvzY6GtTiYwv0rV_KpgqmA6z_Ph6QN9oKMw7bepgummqmD6xkWIaxBlCUSpCG8XFJvdnWXKl7iBRbEe-RJfcEEHO6Is7MLxHTliEYVt5rivwh6rUHU27nXGlGLpddXKdbMxfcfx_136NvAvAAD__4Jwj3Y) for outdoor sports and marching band beginning Aug. 1, under a formal University Interscholastic League (UIL) rule change. ---
| | Oil prices fell sharply after a pause in fighting between the US and Iran, the biggest decline since early April. Brent futures, the global benchmark, closed down 11.3%; US crude dropped about 7%. The –11.3% Brent decline on Monday is the second largest single-day oil price drop of 2026 — behind only the –15% on April 8 when the first ceasefire was announced. The math: Brent was at $102 Thursday, at $90 Monday morning open, and closed Monday at approximately $89–90. The $12 decline from Thursday's peak reflects the war-premium deflating as the bilateral US-Iran pause holds. But oil did not return to $74 — the EIA's Q3 forecast — because the pause is not a ceasefire, Hormuz is still "well below pre-war levels," Kazakhstan's CPC pipeline is still suspended, and the Houthis are still striking Saudi Aramco infrastructure. Even if the Strait of Hormuz is opened, oil experts note that opening will only be partial, with significant damage to infrastructure, refineries and pipelines across the Gulf, ongoing security challenges for tanker traffic, and depleted inventories.
---
| | The oil price at any given moment in July 2026 contains three distinct premiums: the war-continuation premium (conflict is active and escalating), the Hormuz-closure premium (physical supply is disrupted regardless of military activity), and the structural-damage premium (the Gulf's energy infrastructure has been physically hit and needs repair). Monday's –11.3% deflated the war-continuation premium. The Hormuz-closure premium and the structural-damage premium remain intact. The August 11 STEO, now 14 days away, will be the first document to disentangle all three. The EIA's Brent Q3 forecast of $74 — written when all three premiums were near zero — is still structurally $15–20 below where oil will likely settle even if a full ceasefire is announced, because the physical repair of the Gulf's energy infrastructure is measured in months. "Even if the Strait of Hormuz is opened, opening will only be partial." That sentence is the floor under oil prices that no ceasefire announcement can quickly dissolve.
